fullPassage: Semiotics is the theory of signs. Simply put, a sign is something that represents something else. Here's an example: look out of the window and find a tree. There are all sorts of signs for that thing you're looking at. One of them is the word tree itself, four letters spelled out on the page: t-r-e-e. A different sign is the spoken word, "tree." Another sign is a drawing of a tree. A little plastic toy tree is also a sign for 'tree'. Yet another sign is gestural: if you were playing charades and stood straight with your legs together and your arms spread out in a V-shape over your head, your team might guess that you were representing a tree. So signs take the form of words, images, sounds, gestures, objects, even ideas—the thought "tree" generated in your head by looking out of the window is also a sign. But although almost anything has the potential to be a sign, it can only function as a sign if it is interpreted as a sign.

questions.passage: Semiotics is the theory of signs. Simply put, a sign is something that represents something else. Here's an example: look out of the window and find a tree. There are all sorts of signs for that thing you're looking at. One of them is the word tree itself, four letters spelled out on the page: t-r-e-e. A different sign is the spoken word, "tree." Another sign is a drawing of a tree. A little plastic toy tree is also a sign for 'tree'. Yet another sign is gestural: if you were playing charades and stood straight with your legs together and your arms spread out in a V-shape over your head, your team might guess that you were representing a tree. So signs take the form of words, images, sounds, gestures, objects, even ideas—the thought "tree" generated in your head by looking out of the window is also a sign. But although almost anything has the potential to be a sign, it can only function as a sign if it is interpreted as a sign.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마지막 문장 핵심: 'almost anything has the potential to be a sign'(잠재력) + 'if it is interpreted as a sign'(해석 조건) — 요지.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 잠재력(potential) + 해석 조건(interpreted) = 마지막 문장의 핵심 논지 — 글 전체 요지 ←정답

❌ ② 기호는 words, images, sounds, gestures, objects, ideas 등 다양 — '언어만'은 거짓

❌ ③ 나무는 예시일 뿐, 기호학은 모든 기호를 연구 — '자연물만'은 거짓

❌ ④ ideas(생각)도 기호 가능 → 물리적 형태가 '가장 중요'한 조건이 아님
det.tip: 요지 = 마지막 문장 although절: 잠재력(potential) + 해석(interpreted) = 기호 기능의 2가지 핵심.

ch: 거의 모든 것이 기호의 잠재력을 지니지만, 해석이라는 조건이 충족되어야만 기호로 기능할 수 있다.
기호는 언어를 통해서만 전달될 수 있으며, 비언어적 표현은 진정한 기호가 아니다.
기호학은 나무와 같은 자연물만을 연구 대상으로 삼는 학문 분야이다.
사물이 기호가 되려면 물리적 형태를 갖추는 것이 가장 중요한 조건이다.
